differences.design_x: Keeps the brief's 3-minute session everywhere: options step says 180 seconds, prototype flow runs 0:00–3:00, build plan sets timeLimit 180.
differences.design_y: Options step states 150 seconds, prototype flow ends at 2:30, and build plan sets timeLimit 150 — the game only fills 2.5 of the 3 minutes the creator specified.
differences.evidence: Design X build plan: timeLimit 180 with rules 'walk only, no running'. Design Y build plan: timeLimit 150 and flow ending 'wait for others or the 150 seconds run out'. The brief says session_minutes 3.

differences.design_x: Build plan buffers the two trees at normalized (0.46,0.18) and (0.73,0.16), keeps 1.2 m corridors and 0.6 m boundary margin, and keeps spectators outside the course — but never addresses real Songkran water near headsets.
differences.design_y: Does all of the same (trees as 'hard exclusion zones', 1.2 m corridor, 0.6 m margin, spectators outside the south edge) and additionally requires a dry play area isolated from real splashing water, raised from the options-step risk that VR kits are not waterproof, and repeated in the build plan ('the booth isolated from real splashing water').
differences.evidence: Design Y options step risk: 'outdoor Songkran risks splashing water and slippery floors; VR sets are not waterproof, need a dry area separate from real water play'; build plan: 'on a dry 10 x 10 m outdoor temple forecourt'. Design X has no equivalent in any step.

differences.aspect: Cultural respect (เคารพวัด constraint)
differences.design_x: Avoids sacred symbols as targets/obstacles and uses jasmine, water bowls, sand pagodas and flags — respectful but purely decorative.
differences.design_y: Same exclusions (no Buddha images or monks as props) plus makes respect part of the play arc: the final checkpoint is a calm water-pouring blessing ('รดน้ำขอพรอย่างสงบ') before the portal, and the test questions ask whether the blessing scene 'feels calm and respectful'.
differences.evidence: Design Y prototype decision: 'end with a calm water-pouring blessing'; build plan: 'Preserve... the calm visual change at CP6 before the celebratory finish'. Design X prototype decisions only list respectful motifs.

differences.aspect: Specificity and buildability of the final plan
differences.design_x: Layout brief uses normalized coordinates ('x right and y down') for spawn, 6 checkpoints, portal and trees — usable, but requires an extra conversion step and never states the real-world metre positions.
differences.design_y: Layout brief gives actual metre coordinates 'measured in metres from the north-west corner with x east and y south' for spawn, all six checkpoints, the portal, all three hazards, and both trees, and instructs to 'verify their measured positions before placement'.
differences.evidence: Design Y build plan: 'spawn (1.0,8.2); CP1 ... at (1.8,5.2) ... trees at approximately (4.0,4.2) and (6.0,6.2)'. Design X build plan: 'spawn (0.12,0.78), checkpoint 1 ... (0.24,0.60)' with no metre mapping.

differences.design_x: 180-second limit, six checkpoints, scoring (100/-25/300) and the climax of two slippery hazards are identical in options, prototype and build plan.
differences.design_y: Mostly consistent, but the options step promises 'สายน้ำมงคล' ends 'ด้วยภาพรดน้ำขอพร' and the spectator view in the options step says spectators see players 'วิ่งเข้าเส้นชัย' (run to the finish) while later steps forbid running; also the flow says the last dodge is at 1:50 yet the limit is 150 s, leaving the climax timing tight against the cutoff.
differences.evidence: Design Y options spectator_view: 'วิ่งเข้าเส้นชัยด้วยท่าทางชัดเจน' vs build plan rule 'เดินด้วยจังหวะปลอดภัยและไม่วิ่ง'. Design X has no such contradiction.

differences.design_x: Spectators stand on the south side near start and finish, watch the climax dodge and portal finish, and can call directions; stated in options, prototype and build plan.
differences.design_y: Same arrangement: south-side spectators outside the play area watch the final puddle dodge, the blessing scene and the portal finish, with a live leaderboard.
differences.evidence: Both build plans place the climax and finish portal facing the south-side audience and keep spectators outside the course.

differences.design_x: Simple walk-and-dodge race with six ordered checkpoints, three hazard circles, scoring and time bonus — shallow but instantly readable for first-time VR tourists.
differences.design_y: Essentially the same loop (six ordered checkpoints, three puddle hazards, identical 100/-25/300 scoring) with a different skin and a calm ending beat.
differences.evidence: Both build plans: touch 6 points in order, stepping on a red circle costs 25 points and returns you to the last checkpoint, portal gives 300 plus time bonus.

improvements: Design X should add a real-world safety note about water: the venue is an outdoor Songkran event, so the plan should require a dry, splash-isolated play area and headset protection, as Design Y does.
Design X should convert its normalized coordinates into real metres (or state the mapping) in the layout brief so builders can place content without an extra calculation.
Design Y should extend the time limit to the full 180 seconds from the brief (or justify the shorter round) and use the remaining time for the calm blessing beat it advertises.
Design Y should fix the options-step spectator description that says players 'run to the finish', which contradicts its own no-running safety rule.

Both designs could state how the four simultaneous players are physically separated in one 10 x 10 m courtyard (staggered starts or quadrant assignment), since both rely on 'separate copies' without addressing real-body collisions.
summary: Both sessions converge on nearly the same game: a four-player walking race through six Songkran-themed checkpoints with red hazard circles, identical scoring, and a flower-portal finish facing the spectators. Design X is more internally consistent and matches the brief's 3-minute session exactly (180 s everywhere). Design Y is more specific and safer: it gives real metre coordinates, treats the trees as verified hard exclusion zones, adds a dry-area requirement to protect non-waterproof headsets at a real water festival, and weaves the 'respect the temple' constraint into the play arc with a calm water-pouring blessing finale. Design Y's main flaw is shortening the round to 150 seconds against the 3-minute brief, plus a minor contradiction about running in its options step. On balance Design Y's safety and specificity advantages outweigh its timing slip, which is trivially fixable.
why: Design Y wins on the aspects that most affect a real deployment at an actual Songkran event: it is the only one that addresses water exposure to headsets and slippery ground (dry play area, isolated booth), it specifies the build in real metres with tree positions to be verified on site, and it turns the 'respect the temple' constraint into an actual gameplay beat (the calm blessing at CP6) rather than only an art restriction. Design X is cleaner on consistency and hits the 3-minute brief exactly, but its normalized coordinates and missing water-safety handling leave more work and more risk for the operator. Design Y's 150-second timing contradicts the brief but is a one-number fix, whereas Design X's omissions are structural.
x_weaknesses: No mention anywhere of protecting players or headsets from real splashing water at an outdoor Songkran venue, despite the brief's outdoor temple-fair setting.
Layout brief uses normalized coordinates only, with no metre conversion, making on-site placement less direct.
Cultural respect is handled only as an art restriction (avoid sacred symbols); it is not expressed as part of the experience.
Tree positions are given as fixed normalized points with no instruction to verify them against the real trees before building.
y_weaknesses: Cuts the session to 150 seconds in all three steps, contradicting the brief's 3-minute session length.
Options-step spectator view says spectators watch players 'run to the finish', contradicting the no-running safety rule in its own build plan.
The climax dodge is scheduled at 1:50 of a 150-second round, leaving almost no buffer before the time cutoff.
Slightly lower self-scored buildability (4 vs Design X's 5 in the options step) due to needing on-site tree measurement.
